records.source: **Nothing is re-fitted.** The screen reads a coefficient table a regression run already wrote and wraps it in :class:`spacr.profiler.FittedLinear`, which is *reading* the fit. A profiler that re-fits is showing a second model under the first one's name, and on a penalised backend with ``alpha='auto'`` it is not even the same model. records.label: spacr.runctx#2
records.source: **One run id, on every log line and every output.** A run used to be untraceable. The log said a field failed; the registry said an artifact existed; nothing connected them, so "show me everything from the run that produced this file" had no answer. :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per-run JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, which is the whole point.
records.context: **One processing-session id, on every log line and every output.** A processing session used to be untraceable. The log said a field failed; the registry said an artifact existed; nothing connected them, so "show me everything from the processing session that produced this file" had no answer. :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per processing session JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, which is the whole point.
records.translation: **Eitt auðkenni vinnslufundar, á hverri skráar línu og hverju úttaki.** Vinnslufundur var áður ómögulegt að rekja. Dagbókin sagði að reitur mistókst; skráningin sagði að listi væri til; ekkert tengdi þau, svo „sýndu mér allt frá vinnslufundinum sem framleiddi þessa skrá“ hafði ekkert svar. :func:`run_context` býr til eitt auðkenni, stimplar það á hvert :class:`logging.LogRecord` sem er búið til hvert sem er í ferlinu, skrifar JSONL dagbók fyrir hvern vinnslufund sem :func:`read_run_log` les aftur, og afhendir *sama* auðkennið til :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. Ská línu og úttak er því hægt að tengja á ``run_id``, sem er allt punkturinn.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview#3
records.source: **Units.** The assay converts pixels per frame into physical units with ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` and only when *both* are known; otherwise it reports ``px/frame``. A preview that printed "velocity 4.2" while the user was thinking in µm/s would be worse than printing nothing, so the calibration fields start **unset**, every velocity carries its unit, and while the calibration is unknown the panel says so in words instead of quietly borrowing the 1.78 px/µm default.

records.label: spacr.qt.linked_selection.LinkedSelection.unregister_object_opener#2
records.source: Compared with ``==``, not ``is``. The pattern this module documents — ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in the constructor and ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in ``closeEvent`` — hands over a *different bound-method object* each time, because Python builds a new one on every attribute access. Under an identity check that made every withdrawal a silent no-op, so the process-wide registry kept a reference to a destroyed screen and the next ``open_objects`` reached it. Bound methods compare equal exactly when their ``__self__`` and ``__func__`` match, which is the question being asked; anything that does not define ``__eq__`` (a lambda, a ``partial``) still falls back to identity, so the two-screen guarantee above is unchanged.
records.context: Compared with ``==``, not ``is``. The pattern this module documents — ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in the constructor and ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in ``closeEvent`` — hands over a *different bound-method object* each time, because Python builds a new one on every attribute access. Under an identity check that made every withdrawal a silent no-op, so the process-wide registry kept a reference to a destroyed application view and the next ``open_objects`` reached it. Bound methods compare equal exactly when their ``__self__`` and ``__func__`` match, which is the question being asked; anything that does not define ``__eq__`` (a lambda, a ``partial``) still falls back to identity, so the two-application view guarantee above is unchanged.
records.translation: Borið saman við ``==``, ekki ``is``. Mynstrið sem þessi eining skráir — ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` í smiðnum og ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` í ``closeEvent`` — skilar *ólíkum bundnum aðferðahlutum* í hvert sinn, því Python býr til nýjan við hvert aðgang að eiginleika. Undir auðkennisprófi sem gerði allt úttekt að þögðu engri aðgerð, hélt skráning yfir allt ferli áfram tilvísun í eyðilagða forritssýn og næsta ``open_objects`` náði til hennar. Bundnar aðferðir bera saman jafngildi nákvæmlega þegar ``__self__`` og ``__func__`` passa saman, sem er spurningin sem verið er að spyrja; allt sem skilgreinir ekki ``__eq__`` (lambda, ``partial``) fellur samt til auðkennis, svo tveggja-forritssýnarábyrgðin hér að ofan breytist ekki.

records.label: spacr.power_simulate#15
records.source: 1. **``imaging_n_cells_per_well`` did not exist.** ``R/fit_model.R`` reads ``well_data$imaging_n_cells_per_well[1]`` as the Poisson offset, but ``simulate_imaging_plate`` emits only ``..._mu``, ``..._var`` and ``..._gene_per_well``; R's ``$`` partial matching is ambiguous across those three and yields ``NULL``, so the offset column vanishes and the simulate → fit path does not run as committed. :func:`simulate_imaging_plate` emits the column for real, as the realised per-well cell total. 2. **Reads per well were divided by the gene count, not the well count.** ``round(n_reads_total / nrow(well_data))`` groups by well, so ``nrow`` is the library size; with 452 genes and ``n_reads_total = 128318`` that is 284 reads per well against a real screen near 3e4. The parameter was also documented as "total reads" in one vignette and "geometric mean of well reads" in another. :func:`simulate_sequencing_plate` takes an unambiguous ``n_reads_per_well`` and derives ``n_reads_total``. 3. **The hypergeometric draw size could exceed the urn.** Upstream guards ``rmvhyper`` with ``k = min(n_cells_in_well * pcr_factor, n_reads_per_well)``, but the urn is ``round(cells * pcr)`` computed **element-wise**, whose sum is not ``round(sum(cells) * pcr)``. The guard here is computed from the actual colour vector. 4. **The COM-Poisson branch is unusable.** ``COMPoissonReg::rcmp`` is called but not declared in the R package's ``DESCRIPTION``, and has no maintained Python equivalent inside spaCR's dependency set. :func:`sample_count_mean_variance` replaces the ``nu`` dispersion knob with a mean/variance pair dispatched to negative-binomial / Poisson / binomial, which spans the same over-, equi- and under-dispersed range in closed form with no new dependency. Third and higher moments differ from COM-Poisson; nothing upstream used them.
records.context: 1. **``imaging_n_cells_per_well`` did not exist.** ``R/fit_model.R`` reads ``well_data$imaging_n_cells_per_well[1]`` as the Poisson offset, but ``simulate_imaging_plate`` emits only ``..._mu``, ``..._var`` and ``..._gene_per_well``; R's ``$`` partial matching is ambiguous across those three and yields ``NULL``, so the offset column vanishes and the simulate → fit path does not run as committed. :func:`simulate_imaging_plate` emits the column for real, as the realised per-well cell total. 2. **Reads per well were divided by the gene count, not the well count.** ``round(n_reads_total / nrow(well_data))`` groups by well, so ``nrow`` is the library size; with 452 genes and ``n_reads_total = 128318`` that is 284 reads per well against a real screening experiment near 3e4. The parameter was also documented as "total reads" in one vignette and "geometric mean of well reads" in another. :func:`simulate_sequencing_plate` takes an unambiguous ``n_reads_per_well`` and derives ``n_reads_total``. 3. **The hypergeometric draw size could exceed the urn.** Upstream guards ``rmvhyper`` with ``k = min(n_cells_in_well * pcr_factor, n_reads_per_well)``, but the urn is ``round(cells * pcr)`` computed **element-wise**, whose sum is not ``round(sum(cells) * pcr)``. The guard here is computed from the actual colour vector. 4. **The COM-Poisson branch is unusable.** ``COMPoissonReg::rcmp`` is called but not declared in the R package's ``DESCRIPTION``, and has no maintained Python equivalent inside spaCR's dependency set. :func:`sample_count_mean_variance` replaces the ``nu`` dispersion knob with a mean/variance pair dispatched to negative-binomial / Poisson / binomial, which spans the same over-, equi- and under-dispersed range in closed form with no new dependency. Third and higher moments differ from COM-Poisson; nothing upstream used them.
records.translation: 1. **``imaging_n_cells_per_well`` var ekki til.** ``R/fit_model.R`` les ``well_data$imaging_n_cells_per_well[1]`` sem Poisson fært., en ``simulate_imaging_plate`` sendir aðeins frá sér ``..._mu``, ``..._var`` og ``..._gene_per_well``; hlutbundin samsvörun ``$`` í R er tvíræða yfir þessa þrjá og skilar ``NULL``, svo að fráviks dálkurinn hverfur og herma → passa leiðin keyrir ekki eins og ætlað var. :func:`simulate_imaging_plate` sendir dálkinn fyrir alvöru, sem raunverulega heild farsíma á hverja brunn. 2. **Lestrar á brunn voru deildir með genatali, ekki brunnatali.** ``round(n_reads_total / nrow(well_data))`` hópar eftir brunn, svo ``nrow`` er bókasafnsstærðin; með 452 genum og ``n_reads_total = 128318`` sem er 284 lestrar á brunn á móti raunverulegu skimunartilraun nær 3e4. Breytan var einnig skráð sem "total reads" í einni kennslugrein og „stærðfræðilegt meðaltal brunalestra“ í annarri. :func:`simulate_sequencing_plate` tekur ótvírætt ``n_reads_per_well`` og dregur ``n_reads_total``. 3. **Stærð tilviljunarkennds úrtaks gæti farið yfir krukkuna.** Upstream varðveislur ``rmvhyper`` með ``k = min(n_cells_in_well * pcr_factor, n_reads_per_well)``, en urna er ``round(cells * pcr)`` reiknuð **stak-fyrir-stak**, þar sem summa hennar er ekki ``round(sum(cells) * pcr)``. Gæslan hér er reiknuð út frá raunverulegum litavigri. 4. **COM-Poisson greinin er ónothæf.** ``COMPoissonReg::rcmp`` er kölluð en ekki tilgreint í ``DESCRIPTION`` R-pakkans, og hefur engan viðhaldan Python jafngildi innan spaCR's háðar sett. :func:`sample_count_mean_variance` kemur í stað ``nu`` dreifingarhjólsins með meðalfalla/dreifni pör sem send eru til neikvæðra tvíbaugadeilda / Poisson / tvíbaugadeilda, sem spannar sama yfir-, jöfnu- og undirdreifða svið í lokuðu formi án nýrrar háðs. Þriðja og hærri augnablik eru önnur en hjá COM-Poisson; ekkert fyrir ofan notaði þau.

records.label: spacr.qt.shutdown#1
records.source: ``RunRegistry.cancel_all`` is cooperative: it sets a flag, interrupts the thread, and waits. That is the right default -- a pipeline killed mid-write leaves a half-written ``.npy`` or a database row with no rows behind it, and recovering from that costs more than waiting. But cooperative cancellation has one failure mode with no way out from inside the application: a worker that is wedged in a C extension never checks the flag, so it never stops, and ``closeEvent`` refuses to close for as long as it lives.
records.context: ``RunRegistry.cancel_all`` is cooperative: it sets a flag, interrupts the independent execution path, and waits. That is the right default -- a workflow killed mid-write leaves a half-written ``.npy`` or a database row with no rows behind it, and recovering from that costs more than waiting. But cooperative cancellation has one failure mode with no way out from inside the application: a worker that is wedged in a C extension never checks the flag, so it never stops, and ``closeEvent`` refuses to close for as long as it lives.
records.translation: ``RunRegistry.cancel_all`` er samstarfsfús: það setur fána, truflar sjálfstæða keyrsluleið og bíður. Það er rétt sjálfgefið -- vinnuflæði sem er stöðvað miðja skrárgerð skilur eftir sig hálfskrifað ``.npy`` eða gagnagrindarröð án baklaga, og að ná sér af því kostar meira en að bíða. En samstarfsfús afbókun hefur eitt bilunarmynstur með engin úrræði innan forritsins: vinnari sem er fastur í C viðbót athugar aldrei fánann, svo hann hættir aldrei, og ``closeEvent`` neitar að lokast svo lengi sem hann lifir.
